Entities / Places / Ponte Bassa

The Ponte Bassa

Overview

The Ponte Bassa is a canal-side tavern built into the bridge-level masonry at the main Calveno crossing. It is the kind of place people go to eat cheaply in public view of the canal, which in Calveno means in public view of everyone.

At a Glance

FieldDetail
TypeTavern and inn
Location[[calveno
Operated By[[oleandro-fuschi
Public AccessOpen
Known ForFish broth, cheap wine, and a proprietor who knows every boat that has moored here in two decades

Description

The low ceiling on the canal side is where the bridge arch comes down; the back half of the room has clearance. Seating is open to the water — anyone on a passing boat can see who is eating and with whom, which most Calveno regulars treat as a feature. The kitchen smells of fish stock and cheap wine. Upstairs: beds, basic, available by the night.

People & Operations

Proprietor: Oleandro Fuschi — Wide-shouldered, green-grey, soft-spoken. Keeps a mental ledger of every vessel that has moored at the bridge canal in twenty years; he has never been caught wrong about one. If you’re looking for someone who came through Calveno recently, Oleandro either knows or knows who would.

Stock / Services

  • 3 sp — Fish broth — “Bowl, not cup. Bread comes with it.”
  • 5 sp — Grilled canal eel — “House specialty. It’s an acquired taste.”
  • 4 sp — Preserved meat plate — “Salted pork, olives, hard cheese. For sitting over a long conversation.”
  • 2 sp — Cheap wine, carafe
  • ask — House spirits — “Comes in a clay cup. No label.”
  • 2 sp — Bed, shared room — “Three per room.”
  • ask — Canal boat hire — “Two boats. Half-day or full day. I don’t ask where you’re going.”

Current Hooks

  • A captain left a sealed letter with Oleandro three weeks ago “for the next person asking.” He has not opened it.
